newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 4.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 4.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open to large ships on Wednesday even as Tropical Storm Andres was due to land on the southern Pacific Coast, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.

Strong winds along the Pacific Coast shut the largely tourist ports of Huatulco and Puerto Madero to smaller tourism and fishing craft. Crude port Salina Cruz, which ships to the Far East a few times a week, reopened to smaller ships.
The SCT warned ships of high winds and waves along the coasts of Chiapas and Oaxaca.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
Winds in the north from 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) and waves four to six feet high.

Along the southern coast, Andres was causing electric storms and rains along the shores of Oaxaca and Chiapas states. Winds in the Gulf of Tehuantepec from 25 to 55 knots (47 to 104 km/28 to 61 miles per hour) with waves eight to 12 feet high.
Tropical Storm Andres expected to hit ground by 1800 local (2300 GMT) and affect cities along the southern Chiapas state coastline and Guatemala's northern Pacific coast.

Andres bringing light rains and clouds along coast. Winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per day) and up to 20 knots along the coast of Tabasco and the Yucatan peninsula with waves measuring three to six feet high.
Hot and partly cloudy with scattered rains. Winds from 20 to 30 km per hour with gusts of up to 35 km.
